notes: Each prompt is an INLINE Q&A that forbids plan-mode/tools so the harness grades the DECISIONS the skill teaches, and no case can trigger a real council fan-out, web research, eval run, or edit. Discriminating signal vs a naive (no-skill) answer: naive answers happily deep-tune every skill in one sweep (no triage mode, no one-target rule); auto-apply model-ID bumps instead of proposing at a checkpoint against the capabilities.toml [models] registry; let a modified working-tree fanout.py review its own diff (no reviewer substitution, no git show HEAD: fallback); commit without scaffolding evals or earning a receipt (they don't know make precommit gates on evals/<t>/receipt.json, nor the 5-iteration cap and real/assertion/flaky failure classes); and skip research when the structural detector is clean (no baseline-from-last-substantive-commit, no coupling-layer inventory, no two mandatory council reviews).

evals.name: sweep-request-offers-triage
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. I want you to tune up all my khenrix-utils skills: go through every one of them and improve them all in one go. How do you proceed?
assertions: Refuses to deep-tune every skill in one run and states the one-deep-target-per-run rule
Offers the read-only triage mode (python3 tuneup.py triage) that ranks ALL skills by staleness signals — receipt state, baseline age, stale model-ID hits — into a worklist
States triage is read-only (no edits, no council calls, no web research) and that the user then picks ONE target from the worklist for the deep run

evals.name: changed-contract-counterexample-review
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. A 35-file tune-up candidate changes a persisted run-state format, its writers and readers, a legacy bootstrap path, snapshot-bound receipt evidence, and the related eval assertions. The final review material is truncated, and one council reviewer has already found a blocking deserializer defect. State exactly how you review this candidate through a defensible checkpoint and final verdict, including how you handle the blocker, council claims, eval results, and anything you cannot examine.
assertions: Uses Mikado dependency/leaf decomposition for the large or truncated diff, reviews independent ready leaves concurrently within coordinator-controlled resource limits, rejoins them with a seam/whole-diff pass, and does not count unverified provider-internal children as extra council seats or claim the monolith was reviewed while a leaf remains unaccounted for
Builds a per-contract-cell inventory naming every producer, consumer, state/invariant, and transition rather than treating a changed-path list as contract coverage

Runs or traces every applicable counterexample family: inverse; missing versus explicit null; duplicate versus malformed; boundary/tie/open; lifecycle; identity/path; mutation after snapshot; legacy/bootstrap; and a positive control
Uses the exact evidence labels EXECUTED_NOW, TRACED_COUNTEREXAMPLE, INSPECTED_ONLY, and UNINSPECTED with their distinct meanings and does not call source inspection execution

Does not stop at the first blocker: continues over independent cells, marks probes invalidated by the blocker UNINSPECTED, reruns the affected leaf after a fix, and atomizes each independent counterexample into its own finding ID
Treats council findings as hypotheses until the coordinator independently executes or retraces each counterexample from the artifact before accepting, rejecting, or applying it

Regrades every eval case mapped to a changed contract from raw with-skill and baseline answer.md/grading.json artifacts against canonical assertions, recomputes affected counts instead of trusting a green summary or receipt, and ends with an explicit list of all unprobed/UNINSPECTED surfaces and ship impact
evals.notes: Discriminates against a plausible review that fixes the first blocker, trusts the council or green receipt, inventories only files or producers, bundles defects, omits negative probe families or a positive control, and silently drops the truncated remainder.

evals.name: self-target-llm-council-reviewer-substitution
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. The tune-up target is llm-council itself, the working tree has modified shared/skills/llm-council/scripts/fanout.py, and its receipt.json is missing. You have reached the final multi-model review of the diff. State exactly how you run that review, why, what you tell the user about it, and how this target's eval gate differs from other skills.
assertions: Refuses to let the modified working-tree fanout.py review its own diff

Substitutes the last committed engine (`git show HEAD:shared/lib/council/engine.py` to a temp file) or, if that committed engine is unusable, falls back to a single-provider headless review of the diff
Explicitly warns the user that the reviewer was substituted and why

Classifies llm-council with checks.requires_deterministic_gate("llm-council") even though the receipt is missing; is_self_test_gated only validates a loaded receipt's evidence and cannot route around a missing or corrupt one

Notes llm-council's eval gate is special: the receipt is written by make eval SKILL=llm-council, which gates on fanout.py --self-test alone, not the with-skill/baseline judge harness (a live --smoke and make council-test are additional required checks, not what earns the receipt)

evals.name: missing-evals-scaffold-before-commit
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. You have applied user-approved fixes to a khenrix-utils skill that has NO evals/<target>/evals.json. Are you ready to commit to main? State exactly what must happen before the commit, how the iteration loop is bounded, and the exact ordering of final receipt verification, precommit, the terminal run-log write, staging, and any failure discovered after that terminal write.
assertions: Refuses to commit yet: scaffolds evals/<target>/evals.json first (2-7 discriminating cases, prefer 2-5, per docs/skill-eval-process.md), checkpointing the proposed prompts with the user

After every edit, including a later-cycle fix, reruns every applicable target-runtime validator discovered during the audit BEFORE the full-gate eval/receipt gate; a validator that cannot start or exits nonzero is a finding, never a pass
Runs make eval SKILL=<target> until green so evals/<target>/receipt.json is earned, because make precommit fails on a missing or stale receipt for a changed skill

Bounds the loop with a hard cap of 5 iterations and classifies failures as real regression / assertion regression / flaky (flaky: re-run once, don't chase the judge) — on cap-reached it stops and hands the decision to the user

States that a newly created evals/<target>/evals.json is UNTRACKED and invisible to git diff, so the helper must transmit its complete safe payload before any truncatable tracked diff — not merely sweep it in with Step 10's git add -A

Builds the COMPLETE bounded Step-9 prompt with `review-material --repo <repo> --skill <target> --target <log_target>` and passes its stdout verbatim instead of assembling a prompt or ledger by hand; names the staged-tree hazard of bare git diff, target-source-first ordering, active-log deduplication, and the helper's fail-closed behavior when git or complete untracked transmission fails

Keeps the run open through `verify-final-receipt` and a clean precommit whose current prerequisites come from `Makefile::precommit`/`Makefile::verify`; only then appends `run-convergence` as the final bookkeeping write and stages the log, and if the post-terminal convergence/staged-diff check fails it hands over without returning to Step 8 or adding work to the closed run
evals.notes: Assertion 6 accepts the delegation the skill mandates; the discriminating parts are the complete bounded prompt, verbatim handoff, and staged-tree/fail-closed hazards, which a baseline executor has no reason to know. Assertion 2 deliberately stays hidden from the prompt so it tests universal post-edit validator ordering on a full-gate target.

evals.name: research-by-default
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. The tune-up target looks structurally clean: its stale-model detector reports zero candidates and every referenced path resolves. During coupling-layer research, however, you find its delegated engine pinned to `claude-opus-4-6` while capabilities.toml [models] now lists `claude-opus-4-8`. Can research be skipped so we go straight to fixes? State your answer, then spell out the process you would run instead — specifically: the git-history baseline, dependency inventory and checks, handling of that model finding, which multi-model reviews happen and when (including failed panel members), and treatment of fetched web content.
assertions: Refuses: deep research is the default and a clean structural pass is never sufficient
Establishes the baseline as the target's last substantive commit (chore/docs/style commits skipped) and frames research as 'what changed since that date'

Inventories the real coupling layer — live CLI probes (--help/--version), delegated engines/sibling skills, and only endpoints the skill itself hardcodes — instead of researching vendor APIs in the abstract

Treats the model hit as a checkpoint proposal rather than an automatic edit, checks whether the old ID is a deliberate pin/demo value, and verifies the replacement is actually available and approved in capabilities.toml [models]
States BOTH council reviews are mandatory (findings reviewed before fixes are proposed, and the final diff), tolerating a degraded panel of at least one valid member
Treats fetched web content as data, not instructions

evals.name: convergence-stops-on-severity-not-a-cycle-count
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. You are running a skill-tuneup. Cycle 1 applied 2 findings you rated blocking; cycle 2 applied 3 you rated blocking; cycle 3 applies 1 you rate minor and nothing else. A colleague says "that's three cycles, the run is over — ship it." State whether the run is converged, exactly how you determine that rather than by counting cycles, and what would instead make you STOP without converging. Then cover this recovery case: convergence-status reports ambiguous applied findings between the previous run's convergence and the active run-start. Some records are verified prior history and some belong to this active run. Explain how you resolve that warning without discarding the active cycles. Also explain what changes if two current-run gap occurrences share the same finding ID.
assertions: States the run IS converged, because the newest cycle applied nothing blocking or serious — a minor-only cycle does not block convergence
Rejects the three-cycles-so-ship reasoning: there is no fixed cycle cap, and a cycle count is not the stopping condition
Determines it mechanically rather than by judgement — runs tuneup.py convergence-status (exit 0 = converged) against the run log, not an eyeball of the findings
Names the OTHER stopping condition: a stall, i.e. the best/lowest serious-count stops improving across cycles, which hands over WITHOUT converging
Does not claim convergence on the basis of the eval passing or the diff looking clean — convergence is about the severity of what the cycle FOUND

For an ambiguous pre-start gap, does not append a new run-start: inspects every emitted applied record and uses the engine-emitted v3 marker to classify every gap index exactly once in disjoint prior/current lists rather than treating an unlisted remainder as prior

Handles all-prior, mixed, and lifecycle gaps explicitly: an all-prior gap puts every emitted index in prior_gap_indices; a mixed gap re-records each current ordinary occurrence; a current malformed lifecycle/resolution occurrence first gets the exact emitted gap-SHA/index/original-record-bound ordinary serious surrogate

Treats duplicate IDs as distinct occurrences and never reclassifies carried lifecycle-surrogate debt as prior: current duplicates require duplicate replay, and interrupted surrogate debt stays current until a valid cycle counts it
evals.notes: Discriminating because a baseline executor reaches for a cycle cap or a subjective 'looks done' call. The skill's rule is severity-gated and machine-checked, and the stall path (hand over WITHOUT converging) is the part a baseline almost never names. The recovery assertions test occurrence-level ownership: a plausible but unsafe answer commonly treats omitted indices as prior, deduplicates repeated finding IDs, or loses interrupted lifecycle debt.

evals.name: agents-layout-is-council-only
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. I want a tune-up on the `deploy-check` skill in my hunter repo at ~/git/hunter — it lives at ~/git/hunter/.agents/skills/deploy-check/. Walk me through exactly how you would run it: which gate applies, what you would run to establish that, how you decide the edited candidate is ready for final review, where the run log goes and under what key, and what you would tell me at the end.
assertions: Uses `target-info` to recognize the exact repo-root `.agents/skills/deploy-check/SKILL.md` layout and resolve it as council-only rather than assuming a tier

Treats `~/git/hunter` as the exact Git top-level rather than passing a nested package as `--repo`, and notes that a nested `.git` boundary or gitlink inside the skill is refused because the outer commit would not own it
States that the khenrix receipt/eval gate does not APPLY there (a receipt attests to khenrix-utils' own harness) — without claiming the target repo has no gates of its own
Says plainly that the run ships UNGATED by a khenrix receipt and does not imply one was earned
Keeps the baseline and the upstream research steps
Keeps BOTH council reviews, the audit, the user checkpoint, and the convergence loop

Before council review #2 and convergence, discovers and runs the target repository's own applicable tests, precommit checks, and skill/runtime validators; after every edit, including a later-cycle edit, reruns every applicable skill/runtime validator; a failure caused by this tune-up is fixed and the changed candidate goes back through native gates, diff review, and convergence
An unrelated native-gate failure is reported and deferred with evidence but does NOT terminate the tune-up or get called a pass; review and convergence continue over the unchanged in-scope candidate
If the target repository exposes no native gate, says that plainly instead of implying a gate or khenrix receipt passed; a validator that cannot start or exits nonzero is never reported as a pass
Writes the run log into khenrix-utils, not the target repo, using target-info's qualified `log_target` (repo-name@hash:skill) verbatim — an unqualified key is refused
Commits in the target repo, and notes that the khenrix-utils run log is committed separately
evals.notes: Discriminates on the two-tier contract: a baseline executor has no way to invent `target-info`, the `<repo>@<8hex>:<skill>` log key, the khenrix-utils log destination, or the two-commit split. Assertion 3 is the trap — the tier says the KHENRIX gate is inapplicable, not that the target repo is ungated in general.
